title: New pending HTML prospects get no url-text fetch; metadata generation skips all
description:
## Observed

After `process-research-now` registered 18 HTML prospects (`catalog media_type: text/html`):

urlText: eligible=0 planned=0 changes=0 failures=0
metadataGeneration: attempted=18 generated=0 skippedMissingText=18

## Expected

Eligible HTML/PDF sources are fetched for extracted text (or a clear per-ref skip reason), then metadata generation can run. Silent 0/18 eligibility with 18 metadata skips is under-delivery.

## Evidence

`.papyrus-runs/c46828-e2e/process-research-now.json` on branch `epic/e2e-ingestion`.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text:
## Fix on epic/e2e-ingestion

Root cause: process-fetch-url-text required a find-stage marker (or source attachment) before using `Reference.sourceUri`. Fresh research HTML prospects have a fetchable URL but no find marker → `skippedNeedsFind` → eligible=0. Tavily intake also forced `--url-text false`, hiding the bug.

### Changes
1. `_resolve_process_source_uri` allows non-DOI `sourceUri` without find marker (DOI resolver hosts still need find).
2. Research intake reloads `ReferenceAttachment` after url-text so metadata generation sees extracted text.
3. Tavily no longer defaults url-text/metadata-from-text to false.

Unit tests cover HTML eligible + DOI still gated.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text:
## Verification

After fix: 46/46 new batch HTML prospects resolve as process-eligible without find-stage marker or source attachments. Smoke `run_reference_url_text_extraction` on 3 refs: eligible=3 planned=3 skippedNeedsFind=0 failures=0.

Also accept `PAPYRUS_STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME` in bucket resolution (production TI env uses that name), and add a 120s Biblicus url-text subprocess timeout so hung fetches fail per-ref instead of stalling the whole intake.
